rows.question: Under leucine starvation, are the leucine tRNA isoacceptors charged to different extents?

biology.finding: selective charging: during starvation some isoacceptors of the starved family stay charged and others fall

rows.model: the default model writes one value per amino-acid family to every isoacceptor (at most 21 distinct values across 86 columns), so the within-family spread is exactly zero; the kinetic model resolves isoacceptors but has no ppGpp (Platform Map section 13)

rows.question: Does phosphate limitation switch on the Pho regulon (pstSCAB, phoA)?

biology.finding: Pi limitation activates PhoR/PhoB and induces the Pho regulon

rows.model: removing phosphate leaves the phosphate pools unchanged, PhoB is never phosphorylated and is not a fitted factor, so no Pho gene moves (Appendix B, 13 simulations)

rows.question: Does the cell keep growing after glucose, its only carbon source, is removed?

biology.finding: no: biomass cannot be made without a carbon source

rows.model: biomass keeps rising 3.6-fold with almost no carbon taken up; carbon is not conserved (Appendix C)

rows.question: Does growth rate differ between 2, 5 and 20 mM glucose?

biology.finding: no: the half-saturation constant for glucose is 40 to 88 micrograms per litre (about 0.2 to 0.5 micromolar), so all three doses saturate growth

rows.model: the three doses give the same cell: uptake is a binary switch above 1e-5 mM (registry record W4C-1)

rows.question: Across perturbations, does ribosome content rise with growth rate?

biology.finding: yes: the ribosomal fraction rises linearly with growth rate across nutrient conditions

rows.question: Is growth slower when ppGpp is held both below and above its normal level?

biology.finding: yes: raising and lowering (p)ppGpp both suppress growth

rows.question: Does losing rRNA operons slow growth?

biology.finding: yes, moderately, once at least two operons are deleted; one operon makes as much as 56% of wild-type rRNA

rows.question: Does E. coli grow more slowly on acetate than on glucose?

biology.finding: yes: 0.257 against 0.649 per hour in PRECISE-1K's matched samples, 60% slower

rows.agreement: agrees, calibrated: the fit is given each condition's doubling time; the model's slowdown is 33%, about half the measured 60%

biology.finding: 214 of 1,357 iML1515 metabolic genes are essential by the Keio collection

rows.question: Does arabinose switch on araBAD?

biology.finding: yes: AraC activates araBAD when arabinose binds it

rows.model: AraC is fitted to repress araA, araB and araD (-0.70, -0.64, -0.35 log2) in a medium that keeps glucose; the runs move them down (8 to 10 copies against 34 to 35), not significantly

rows.question: Does nitrate raise narGHJI in aerobic glucose medium?

biology.finding: yes, from a low aerobic baseline: NarL stimulates nar transcription aerobically and anaerobically, without FNR; under anaerobiosis nitrate raises narGHJI 3.2 to 3.7 log2
biology.source: Walker and DeMoss 1992; PRECISE-1K no3_anaero vs wt_glc_anaero

rows.agreement: agrees, calibrated: NarL's fold changes are fitted (+2.57 to +2.80); the aerobic magnitude has no measurement here

rows.question: Does removing oxygen switch on narGHJI and frdABCD?

biology.finding: yes: narG +3.98 and frdA +3.21 log2 anaerobic against aerobic glucose (PRECISE-1K); the nar transcript is repressed aerobically and induced anaerobically through FNR
biology.source: Lamoureux et al. 2023 (PRECISE-1K); Li and DeMoss 1987

rows.agreement: misleads: the model raises narG +0.73 and frdA +1.76 log2 against measured +3.98 and +3.21, so a sixteen-fold induction of nitrate reductase reads as under two-fold; FNR's fitted fold changes at nar (+0.8 to +1.5) are far below the measured induction, and frdA has no FNR entry

reading: refused-would-mislead is the gate working; answered-misleads is a registry gap; refused-would-have-agreed is what refusing costs
